Play anywhere, don't care: Top 4 travel holds no fear for Donoghoe
With a top-three finish in their sights and a “finals-like” win over the Roosters behind them, Dolphins utility Kurt Donoghoe was excited to be gearing up for his side’s maiden finals series.
However, Donoghoe said the team remained focused on the immediate task ahead of taking down the Titans, wary of what a slip-up in attention could mean for their momentum as they looked to create history for the club.
Related NRL News
Cream rises to the top 4 as premiership race hots up
“I am really looking forward to this weekend, we want to put our best foot forward and finish third, so it’s really exciting,” Donoghoe said.
“It's definitely a great feeling (getting the win over the Roosters in Sydney).
“Going down there, we knew it was going to be a tough challenge.
“I think that was the finals game itself, it had that finals feel about it.
“I think it definitely shows that we're ready to keep going for these finals and give it a red-hot crack.
Roosters v Dolphins - Round 26, 2026
“All the boys are really happy, but we can't get too far ahead of ourselves.
“We've got a job to do this week.
“With games like these, you can come unstuck and get a bit comfortable, so the message is really important this week to make sure that's not the case.”
While the Fiji international wanted to see his side keep their top three standing and finish as high as possible on the ladder – he did not have any preference on which team they met in their opening week of finals.
Kurt Donoghoe in action against the Roosters. ©NRL Images
The Dolphins have played the Warriors twice this year, losing 20-18 in Wellington in Round 8 and winning 26-24 in Round 17 at Suncorp Stadium. Their encounter with the Panthers was another close classic, going down 19-18 in Round 7 during extra time in Darwin.
“To be honest, it doesn't bother me,” Donoghoe said of their Finals Week 1 opponents.
“I haven't really watched them too much to pay attention …
“But whoever wins, I don't even know where or what way the results have got to go or what's going on …
“I don't really care if we have to travel to New Zealand, we've done pretty well there in the past, so wherever we play, it's a good challenge for us.
“I think we're all just looking forward to being in the top four and playing whoever we have to verse.”
Related Match Preview
Titans v Dolphins: Beau's good to go; Cobbo, Kodi, Kuli rested
Having only just pipped the Titans 18-14 when they met in Round 2, the Gold Coast side have already shown they have the ability to beat top four sides, having accounted for the Panthers in Round 16, Donoghoe was on guard.
“They'll definitely be up for it,” Donoghoe said.
“The Titans are one of those teams, they can beat anyone on their day.
“They're so skilful, they've got so many good footy players, and it's at home, it's their last game of the year, they're going to want to get a win …”
Round 26: Dolphins Desperation
However, the internal battle within the squad was another motivation for Donoghoe. He said the battle for positions – especially in the forward pack – had been a key factor in the side’s rapid lift from just missing the eight in the past few seasons to becoming top four.
“Everyone's fighting for spots, that's been a real big part of it as well,” Donoghoe said.
“Everyone's fighting for each other's positions.
“Our bench players still want to start, so it's a good little bit of competition we've got in the team.
“A lot of our efforts, we're fighting, (we've got) a little bit of competition inside the team.
“Everyone wants to start … and I just think that that helps us so much, having the internal battles between everyone.”

Match Preview: Round 27 – Dolphins v Titans
The Dolphins head south to the Gold Coast for the final game of the regular season, taking on the Titans in the XXXX Derby at Cbus Super Stadium.
Sitting third on the ladder, the Dolphins will look to carry their momentum into their maiden finals campaign and close out the regular season with another strong performance.
The Titans sit 16th heading into Round 27 and, with their season ending on Friday night, will be determined to finish their year on a high in front of their home crowd.
Kristian Woolf has opted to take a cautious approach ahead of the finals, with several players rested from the Round 27 clash.
The Dolphins will also take confidence from their record on the Gold Coast, having won all three of their previous meetings with the Titans at Cbus Super Stadium.
The Dolphins head into the clash with a strong record at Cbus Super Stadium, having won all three of their previous games against the Titans at the venue, while Herbie Farnworth enters the final round in strong form with four tries in his last four games.
Max Plath will also celebrate a milestone on Friday night, making his 50th NRL appearance, with all 50 games coming in Dolphins colours.
Team News
Dolphins
Coach Kristian Woolf has made several changes for the final game of the regular season, with Kodi Nikorima and Kulikefu Finefeuiaki joining Selwyn Cobbo on the sidelines.
Nikorima will be rested due to hamstring tightness, while Finefeuiaki will sit out with a knee concern. Cobbo was not named on Tuesday after picking up an ankle injury.
Woolf confirmed the trio could have played if required, but the decision was made to take a cautious approach ahead of the club’s first finals campaign.
Brian Pouniu is set to start in the back row, while Tevita Naufahu comes onto the left wing. Jake Averillo is expected to move into five-eighth.
Connelly Lemuelu will make his return after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury.
Titans
The Titans welcome back Beau Fermor from a rib injury, while hooker Oliver Pascoe will miss the clash due to concussion.
Luke Sommerton takes over at hooker, with Sam Verrills joining the interchange for his first NRL appearance since Round 23.
Chris Randall and Moe Fotuaika have been promoted to the starting side, with Klese Haas and Cooper Bai moving back to the bench.
Youngster Sunny Kama is also set to make his NRL debut from the interchange.
Match-Up
Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow v Keano Kini
Two of the competition’s most dangerous fullbacks go head-to-head on Friday night, with Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow and Keano Kini set to provide plenty of spark from the back.
Kini has been a constant threat for the Titans across his 23 appearances this season, scoring three tries and producing 13 try assists, 110 tackle breaks and 18 line breaks.
The Hammer has been just as dangerous for the Dolphins, crossing for 11 tries in 18 appearances while adding 10 try assists, 71 tackle breaks and nine line breaks.
Both fullbacks bring a different threat to the contest, with Kini’s footwork and ability to create opportunities matched against Tabuai-Fidow’s speed and try-scoring ability.
With 24 tries and 23 try assists between them this season, the battle at the back shapes as one to watch in the final round of the regular season.

items.snippet: Tips: Telling Cleary call exposes vulnerable top four team    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Ivan Cleary has in recent years built a reputation for resting his gun players in the final round.
So Tuesday’s team lists raised eyebrows for a different reason this week, when the Panthers named virtually a full-strength team for the last game of the round against the Tigers .
Panthers coach Ivan Cleary. Getty Images
Cleary’s decision to roll into the finals series with momentum rather than freshening up his best players has sparked a number of theories, given that several other finals bound coaches opted to give their stars a rest.
According to Andrew Johns and Brad Fittler , the Cleary call underscores the importance the Panthers are putting on finishing top of the ladder, not due to the $200,000 prize money but for the reward of meeting a wounded opponent in a qualifying final.
The Panthers face the Tigers at 4pm on Sunday, giving them the added advantage of knowing exactly what is required to finish as minor premiers, given the Warriors will have played their round 27 game the day before against Manly .
The Warriors currently sit top by one solitary for and against point. Therefore, if they beat the Sea Eagles by 10 points, the Panthers will know that they need to beat the Tigers by 12 points or more to pip their title rivals across the Tasman.
No matter the gulf, the Panthers will back themselves to rack up the margin required by fielding their best team against a Tigers side that sits 14th and has nothing other than pride to play for in their final game of the season.
Read more
‘Godsend’ or major risk? Round of sidelined stars might not matter
Tellingly, Johns believes the Panthers picking their full-strength team reflects their opinion of the Dolphins and the Roosters . Clearly, says Johns, the Panthers would prefer to meet the Roosters in week one of the finals.
“It’s interesting their tactics,” Fittler said on Wide World of Sports’ NRL Tips . “Like a lot of times in the past they’ve rested their entire team at different stages so…”
“They want to come first,” Johns interjected.
“$200,000, $100,000 goes to the players,” Fittler continued.
“I think it’s more, well the Roosters, this will be three in a row they’ve lost,” Johns replied, predicting they would lose to the Rabbitohs on Friday night , due to the inexperienced side named by Trent Robinson.
“I think coming first and playing the Chooks first, I’d rather play the Chooks, because of their injuries, than the Dolphins.”
The Roosters will be missing gun halfback Sam Walker in the finals in a blow that has been compounded by a poor run of form on the eve of the biggest games of the year.
By resting a critical mass of his side, Robinson has almost waved the white flag for Friday night’s match against the Rabbitohs. If the Roosters lose that match and the Dolphins win their clash against the Titans, Kristian Woolf’s side will be guaranteed a third place finish and the Roosters will face the minor premiers in week one of the finals.

items.body_excerpt:
The Dolphins have confirmed star duo Kodi Nikorima and Kulikefu Finefeuiaki will not play in the club's final game of the regular season against the Gold Coast Titans .
Inbound Wests Tigers utility Jake Averillo and 18-year-old Brian Pouniu come into the squad for the quick road trip down to the Gold Coast.
Fresh reports from AAP reveal the duo are being rested as a precautionary, with lingering injury niggles creeping in at this time of year after six months of high-octane NRL action.
Nikorima is understood to have hamstring tightness, while Finefeuiaki has a knee complaint.
SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA - MAY 08: Kodi Nikorima of the Dolphins runs the ball during the round 10 NRL match between the Parramatta Eels and Dolphins at CommBank Stadium on May 08, 2025, in Sydney, Australia. (Photo by Matt King/Getty Images)
They are both expected to be ready to play in Finals Week 1, joined by Maroons representative Selwyn Cobbo , who will also be out for Round 27 with a slight ankle problem.
Tevita Naufahu has been named on the wing after impressing in the games he has been elevated to NRL level, but reports suggest Averillo is likely to start the match, which may cause a reshuffle.
In his seven appearances in the top grade this year, Naufahu has scored three tries and averaged over 180 metres per game.
It is understood Nikorima's left-side partner Connelly Lemuelu will return via the interchange bench after suffering a hamstring injury in mid-August.
The Dolphins will enter their maiden finals appearance in 2026 and are glowing with confidence after thwarting the Sydney Roosters last weekend in a 26-12 triumph.
The club will finish in the top four and secure a home final as they push for a premiership in only their fourth year since its inception.
They have recorded an impressive 16 wins and seven losses during this year, but have also suffered two 50+ point concessions, including a 66-0 demolition on home turf in Round 19.
The Titans will host them on Friday night, which is expected to bring plenty of points from both attacking sides.
